newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hogs seen steady on Monday - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hogs seen steady on Monday - dealers.

text.p: Midwest cash hog prices Monday were seen steady amid expectations for increased marketings, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
Top prices in Iowa and southern Minnesota for hogs delivered to plants could range from $54.00 to $55.00 per cwt and Illinois top prices could match Friday's at $55.00 to $56.00.
Indiana/Ohio buyers expect prices Monday to be steady, with a top of $54.00 to $55.00 at plants.
Prices Friday were up mostly $1.00 from Thursday on strong demand from packers for Saturday operations, sources said.

USDA estimated Saturday's slaughter at 152,000 head, compared with 151,000 a week ago and 135,000 a year ago. The week-to-date estimate was 1.961 million head, which was 3.4 percent larger than a year ago and the largest weekly slaughter since mid-January.

Demand for hogs was fueled by strong demand from retailers planning end-of-month advertising features going into October, deemed National Pork Month by some meat industry groups and supermarket chains, market sources said.
Price strength also was linked to talk that export demand has been picking up, sources said.
